$comment: England & Wales, Animal Law - the objective 'knew or ought reasonably to have known' fault standard under Animal Welfare Act 2006 s.4(1)(b). Fresh research this session, both nodes independently re-fetched and confirmed a second time by the orchestrating session.
verification_method: Animal Welfare Act 2006 s.4(1) fetched live and directly from legislation.gov.uk, independently re-fetched and word-for-word consistent on both attempts. R (Gray & Ors) v Crown Court at Aylesbury [2013] EWHC 500 (Admin) fetched live and directly from Find Case Law, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time.

authorities.name: Animal Welfare Act 2006, s.4
authorities.date_note: Enactment year. The text verified this session is the current in-force version.
authorities.proposition: A person commits an offence if an act of his, or a failure of his to act, causes an animal to suffer (s.4(1)(a)); he knew, or ought reasonably to have known, that the act or failure to act would have that effect or be likely to do so (s.4(1)(b)); the animal is a protected animal (s.4(1)(c)); and the suffering is unnecessary (s.4(1)(d)).
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, on two independent passes, word-for-word consistent both times.

authorities.name: R (Gray & Ors) v Crown Court at Aylesbury
authorities.court: High Court (Queen's Bench Division, Administrative Court)
authorities.judge_or_panel: Toulson LJ (leading judgment), Silber J (concurring, with a separate judgment on the costs appeal)
authorities.proposition: Section 4(1)(b)'s 'knew, or ought reasonably to have known' standard sets an objective fault threshold, not a purely subjective one - it catches negligent conduct as well as deliberate or knowing conduct, rejecting a narrower reading under which only actual foresight would suffice. On the facts, a horse trader whose 115 horses were found severely neglected at Spindle Farm had been properly convicted of 11 offences under the Act, applying that objective standard.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from Find Case Law this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches word-for-word consistent on paragraphs 24 and 26's construction of the s.4(1)(b) fault standard.

edges.verified_via: R (Gray) v Crown Court at Aylesbury [2013] EWHC 500 (Admin), paras 24 and 26, fetched directly from Find Case Law and independently re-confirmed: construes s.4(1)(b)'s 'knew or ought reasonably to have known' language as imposing liability for a negligent act or omission, not only a knowing one.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes covering the objective fault standard for unnecessary suffering. Does not cover s.9's separate duty-to-ensure-welfare offence in detail (though the same case's paras 31 and 43 touch on it, not built out here), licensing of animal activities, wildlife protection legislation, or any other Animal Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
